name: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
summary: Managed Azure service for building and scaling agents as either configuration-defined prompt agents or container-based hosted agents, with the Responses API as the single model and tool entry point. Runtime, tools, Entra identity, tracing, and evaluation live inside a Foundry project; there is no self-hosted distribution.

agent-runtime.note: The Agent Runtime hosts prompt and hosted agents, managing conversations, tool calls, and session state behind a managed autoscaled endpoint.

orchestration.note: Workflows provide a declarative visual builder for multi-agent sequences with branching, variables, and human-in-the-loop approval steps, plus A2A connections.

knowledge-memory.note: The File Search tool indexes uploaded documents into managed vector stores, with an additional memory tool and Azure AI Search grounding available.

tools-integration.note: The tool catalog offers built-in tools, OpenAPI tools, function calling, remote MCP servers, and Toolbox bundling curated tools behind one managed MCP endpoint.

identity-governance.note: Agents can hold a dedicated Microsoft Entra identity with Azure RBAC, integrated guardrails and content filters, per-tool approval requirements, and documented quotas.

observability.note: Agent tracing records every model call and tool invocation with Application Insights integration, service dashboards, and continuous production evaluation.

data-secrets.note: Files and vector stores are service-managed and tool credentials sit in project connections, but durable storage and secrets rely on Azure Storage and Key Vault.

evaluation.note: Evaluations run uploaded JSONL datasets against an agent using rubric, quality, safety, and custom evaluators, returning per-run and per-row scores.

channels.note: Agents publish from the Foundry portal into Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot via a generated Teams manifest and Azure Bot Service channel.

code-execution.note: The Code Interpreter tool executes agent-written Python in a sandbox, with a custom variant allowing configured packages and Container Apps resources.

human-in-loop.note: An MCP tool configured to always require approval emits an approval request item that suspends the tool call until the caller submits a matching approval response.

multi-tenancy.note: A Foundry project scopes agents and Azure RBAC roles with optional per-agent role scopes, but tenancy is plain Azure RBAC on ARM resources rather than an agent-service tenant model.

declarative-deployment.note: Agents and their deployments are first-class ARM resource types authorable in Bicep, ARM JSON, or Terraform, with parent-child dependency resolution and pinned version references.

agent-versioning.note: Saved agent versions are immutable and referenced by name and version, with version history, per-version diffing, request routing to a specific version, and rollback.

skill-learning.note: The preview agent optimizer discovers and refines reusable skills for a hosted agent using datasets generated from its own traces, but a human applies and redeploys the winning candidate.
